title: Instant demo: zero-config SDK pathways (notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Capture a small, reproducible "instant demo" experience that requires zero API keys or sign-in for local eval (uses local sandbox token), so we can show an SDK-powered app in a 3–5 minute walk-through.
- Focus on clarity: one minimal flow per language (shell, Python, Node), one tiny interactive sample app (chat bubble), and one metric to celebrate (latency + cost estimate).

User journey (happy path):
1) Clone repo (1 cmd).
2) Run ./demo up (single script launches a tiny static server + sandbox token).
3) Open http://localhost:8000 — chat UI prewired to Redwood SDK, example prompt prefilled.
4) Click "Send" — streaming response appears within 500ms (goal).

Zero-config components (implementation notes):
- Local sandbox token stored in repo as .sandbox/token (gitignored in real release; for demo keep small ephemeral token mechanism).
- Dockerfile for reproducible env (tiny node static server + Python backend option).
- Fallback flow: if sandbox exhausted, we show recorded streaming playback (UX: "Demo offline — see live capture").

Language pathways (short cheats):
- Shell: curl --header 'Authorization: Sandbox <token>' \
  POST /v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-small-demo","prompt":"Hello from demo"}'
- Python (requests):
  resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Sandbox {token}"})
- Node (fetch):
  const r = await fetch('/api/generate', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload), headers})

Telemetry + badges to highlight in demo UI:
- Request latency (ms) last 10s, displayed in corner.
- Token/response size estimate (approx cost) shown under each response.
- Event: demo_open, demo_send, demo_fallback recorded to analytics.

Failure scenarios to rehearse (prep notes):
- Sandbox rate-limited: UI shows "Try recorded run".
- No network: static demo page still plays recorded sample and greys out send button.
- Schema mismatch: sample server returns 500 — show developer console hint with minimal debugging steps.

Success metrics we want to communicate (during live demo):
- "Cold to first byte" under 700ms on 1-vCPU dev box.
- Example cost estimate: 0.7¢ for the response (explain unit cost briefly).
- Demo engagement: measure clicks on "Open full SDK" and repo clones (tracked via shortlink UTM).

Copy & UX copy snippets (for modal and README):
- Modal title: "Try Redwood in 3 minutes — no signup required"
- Button: "Run demo locally"
- Readme blurb (short): "Clone, run ./demo up, open localhost:8000. No keys, zero config."

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Do we ship a persistent branded sandbox token or generate ephemeral per-download? Pros/cons listed in linked Confluence doc.
- Which model variant to expose for demo? (small demo model vs mid-size with streaming).
- Legal: can we include sandbox token in published demo repo? (talk to legal).

Testing checklist (pre-demo run):
- [ ] ./demo up works on macOS + Ubuntu WSL
- [ ] Fallback playback file present and validated
- [ ] Telemetry events fire to staging channel (DEV-ANALYTICS-STG)
- [ ] README + modal copy finalized

Notes for handoff to docs and demo team:
- Deliverables: tiny repo, 1-minute screen recording, 30s GIF for landing page, README with one-liner to copy into docs landing.
- SRE ask: provide short guide for running demo in CI to catch regressions (weekly smoke).

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Marco: prototype ./demo up scripts and Dockerfile (ETA 2 days).
- Priya: draft README/landing copy and prepare GIF export (ETA 3 days).
- Tomás: wire telemetry stubs to staging and add dashboard widget (ETA 4 days).
- Aisha (me): coordinate legal check and update Confluence page with decisions (ETA EOW).

Quick links / references (in-text):
- Example quickserver code: /examples/instant-demo/server.js
- UX mock: figma://file/InstantDemoMockup (placeholder)
- Related tickets: JIRA-DEVEXP-421, JIRA-SDK-88

Bottom line: aim for a frictionless mini-experience that's robust to offline and rate-limited conditions, easy to replicate during customer calls, and designed to drive repo clones and SDK adoption. This doc is intentionally terse — expand any section into its own PRD when we pick an owner for full launch.

-- end --
